findings.summary: The section does not cover an outline point (missing "language", "standard").
findings.evidence: ES modules (ESM): static import/export, parsed before any code runs; the language standard, works in browsers and Node
findings.fix: Add the point with an explanation and an example.

findings.summary: The section does not cover an outline point (missing "function", "matching").
findings.evidence: Named export: export const a = 1; export function f(){}; import with matching names: import { a, f } from './m.js'
findings.fix: Add the point with an explanation and an example.

findings.summary: Code block is shown after the rules but the page's "Rename, re-export, side effects" section lists several forms without a one-line idea per code line, and one bullet holds two ideas.
findings.evidence: Default and named together: default first, braces after
findings.fix: Annotate each code line with a short comment (rename, re-export named, re-export all, side-effect only, default plus named).

findings.summary: The term TDZ is used without ever being defined, so a learner cannot tell why a circular import gives a ReferenceError.
findings.fix: Add a short gloss, for example: "TDZ (temporal dead zone) = the binding exists but is not yet initialised, so reading it throws ReferenceError".

findings.summary: Circular imports section is plain prose-like bullets for a comparison that would fit the ESM vs CJS table.
findings.evidence: ESM: uninitialised binding → TDZ ReferenceError / CJS: partially filled exports object
findings.fix: Add a 'Circular import' row to the ESM vs CJS table.

findings.summary: Page 3 omits a trailing 'Remember' note and the 'import() vs import' interview answer repeats earlier bullets; also the table on page 1 and page 3 duplicate the live-binding vs value-copy comparison.
findings.evidence: Exports | value copies | live bindings (page 1) and Exports | live view | value copy (page 3)
findings.fix: Keep one comparison table and refer to it, or use the same wording ('live binding' vs 'value copy') in both.

findings.summary: The 'ESM imports CJS' and 'require(esm)' rules are crammed into one stacked list mixing two directions, and the 'exports' section mixes three ideas in terse fragments.
findings.evidence: ESM imports CJS: module.exports = default import / Older Node: require(esm) throws ERR_REQUIRE_ESM / 22.12+/20.19+: sync ESM works; top-level await throws ERR_REQUIRE_ASYNC_MODULE
findings.fix: Split into a small table: Direction | Node version | Result. Put 'exports' fields in their own list before the JSON.

findings.summary: Version thresholds are inconsistent: 20.19+ is cited both for ESM syntax sniffing and for require(esm), and the sniffing line lists different versions than the require line, which is confusing for skimming.
findings.evidence: Node 22.7+/20.19+ sniff ESM syntax when no type; ... 22.12+/20.19+: sync ESM works
findings.fix: Put the version cutoffs in one table row per feature so they are easy to compare.

findings.summary: Bullets mix unrelated ideas and the npm scripts section has orphan rules appended below the table.
findings.evidence: import * as lib or barrels with side effects keep code in the bundle / && chains sequentially; use a cross-platform tool for env vars
findings.fix: Move the namespace/barrel point to the tree-shaking section and add the && note as its own table row or bullet.
